e.title: 坐标级洪水定价微服务：用与水体距离的指数衰减加费替代邮政编码分区，但 README 的公式与示例算的不是同一个函数
e.title_en: A coordinate-level flood pricing microservice that replaces postal-code territory rating with exponential decay on distance to water — though its README formula and its own worked example are not the same function
e.title_hk: 坐標級洪水定價微服務：用與水體距離的指數衰減加費替代郵政編碼分區，但 README 的公式與示例算的不是同一個函數
e.summary: 一个把洪水加费从「邮政编码分区」改到「坐标到最近水体距离」的定价微服务：用 Nominatim 地理编码、OSMnx 取水文几何、投影到 UTM 后用 Shapely 算米级最短欧氏距离，再以指数衰减乘数产生空间加费；README 给出完整公式与分级表，但其头号公式含一个减 10 的偏移，而示例回显的 formula_applied 与算出的 2.72 都不含该偏移
e.summary_hk: 一個把洪水加費從「郵政編碼分區」改到「坐標到最近水體距離」的定價微服務：用 Nominatim 地理編碼、OSMnx 取水文幾何、投影到 UTM 後用 Shapely 算米級最短歐氏距離，再以指數衰減乘數產生空間加費；README 給出完整公式與分級表，但其頭號公式含一個減 10 的偏移，而示例回顯的 formula_applied 與算出的 2.72 都不含該偏移
e.summary_en: A pricing microservice that moves flood surcharging from postal-code territories to the distance between a coordinate and the nearest water body: Nominatim geocoding, OSMnx hydrological geometry, reprojection to UTM and a Shapely shortest Euclidean distance in metres, feeding an exponential-decay multiplier that produces the spatial surcharge; the README gives a complete formula and tier table, but its headline formula carries a minus-ten offset that neither the echoed formula_applied string nor the worked example (which yields 2.72) includes
e.body:
**geo-catastrophe-pricing** 是一个**把洪水加费从邮政编码分区改到坐标到水体距离的定价微服务**（仓库 `Devananditha/geo-catastrophe-pricing`），**实测 ★0、fork 0、主语言 Python、仓库体量 18 KB、创建于 2026-09-08、最后推送 2026-09-09**（**均 GitHub API 实测值，在解冻窗口内**）；**⚠️⚠️ 该仓库实测**无任何许可文件**——`LICENSE`、`LICENSE.md`、`LICENSE.txt`、`license`、`COPYING` 于 main 分支**逐一实测均为 404**，**GitHub API 亦报 `NONE`**——**但其 README 却带有指向 `LICENSE` 的「License: MIT」徽章，且正文「License」一节逐字声称本项目以 MIT 许可发布**（**详见下方标注 ①**）；**无 topics**；**README 实测 7,907 字节**。本条目属于本轮主题**「把假设写成可核对的东西」**中的**第三种：它把评级公式连同参数一起写下来，而写下来的公式与它自己的示例并不一致**。

可核实信息（**均 README 与仓库根目录实测**）：⭐⭐⭐ **根目录实测只有五项**：**`.gitignore`（291 字节）、`README.md`（7,907 字节）、`main.py`（18,846 字节）、`requirements.txt`（59 字节）、`spatial_risk_engine.py`（5,475 字节）**——**即整个实现是**两个 Python 文件****。**README 标题逐字为「Geospatial Catastrophe Pricing Model | Dynamic Flood Risk Engine」**。⭐⭐⭐ **其问题陈述逐字，是本条目最有价值的一段**：**「Traditional Property & Casualty (P&C) underwriting models rely heavily on aggregated territorial rating factors and static postal code boundaries. These coarse macro-level segmentations introduce significant underwriting error: **adjacent structures separated by mere tens of meters can exhibit radically divergent hydrological profiles**, leading to **widespread risk mispricing, adverse selection, and unpriced aggregate exposure**.」**——**即「传统财产险核保模型高度依赖聚合的**地区评级因子**与**静态邮政编码边界**；这种粗粒度的宏观切分带来显著的核保误差：**仅相距数十米的相邻建筑可能拥有截然不同的水文特征**，从而导致**普遍的错误定价、逆选择与未定价的累积暴露**」**。**其四阶段流水线逐字实测**：**物理地址 →（地理编码：Nominatim／GeoPy）WGS84 坐标点（纬经度）→（空间图查询：OSMnx）半径 ≤ 2,000 米内的水文几何 →（度量投影与邻近计算：GeoPandas ＋ Shapely）最短欧氏距离（米）→（乘数评级引擎：指数衰减曲线）动态保费报价**；**其中水文标签逐字为 `{"water": True, "waterway": True}`**，**且「若缓冲半径内不存在任何水体要素，距离按无穷大（∞）处理」**；**投影步骤逐字说明用 `GeoDataFrame.estimate_utm_crs()` 自动确定 UTM 带，以消除按角度坐标直接算欧氏距离带来的纬度相关畸变**。

对 RIAA：**① ⭐⭐⭐ 「相邻数十米的两栋建筑水文特征可能截然不同」这一句问题陈述是本条目写得最好的一处**——**它把「为什么需要坐标级定价」讲成了一个**可检验的核保误差来源****：**静态分区必然产生**区内方差被忽略**与**区界两侧被强行区分**两类错误**；**而洪水恰恰是**空间梯度极陡**的险种**（**可与 [[hazus]]、[[gem-vmtk]]、[[floodmodeller-api]]、[[lisflood]]、[[thinkhazard]]、[[pyincore]] 等洪水与暴露模型并读**；**⚠️ 本词条**不主张**坐标级加费在任何监管框架下都可直接使用**——**分区评级在多数辖区有其监管与统计理由（可信度、可解释性、避免歧视性定价）**）。**② ⭐⭐⭐ **README 里的公式与它自己的示例算的不是同一个函数——这是本条目最需要如实指出的一处****。**README 头号公式逐字为 `Multiplier(d) = 1.0 + 2.0 × exp(−λ(d − 10))`，其中 λ = 1/300**；**而 README 给出的示例响应的 `formula_applied` 字段逐字为 `1.0 + 2.0 * exp(-d / 300.0)`**——**两式的差别正是那个 `−10` 偏移**。⭐⭐ **本词条以两个公式分别复算该示例（距离 45.2 米）**：**含偏移的 `exp(−(d−10)/300)` 得 **2.7786**；不含偏移的 `exp(−d/300)` 得 **2.7203****；**而示例所报 `spatial_multiplier` 为 **2.72**、`final_premium` 为 **3264.0**（**且 1200 × 2.72 = 3264，自洽**）**——**即示例实际走的是**不含偏移**的版本，而正文头号公式写的是含偏移的版本**。⭐⭐ **分级表也印证了这一点**：**表中「≤10 米 → 3.00×」这个最大值只有**含偏移**版本在 d = 10 时才能取到（`exp(0)` → 1 + 2 = 3.00）**；**而表中 11–250 米区间的 1.87×–2.93× 与 251–500 米的 1.38×–1.86×，与**不含偏移**版本的取值吻合**（**本词条实算：d = 11 → 2.9280 ≈ 2.93；d = 250 → 1.8692 ≈ 1.87；d = 500 → 1.3778 ≈ 1.38；d = 999 → 1.0716 ≈ 1.07；d = 1000 → 1.0713**）。⭐⭐⭐ **即：文档里同时存在两个函数，而「最大加费封顶 3.00×」这一说法属于**写了但没被应用**的那一个**（**⚠️ 本词条**不主张**代码里究竟是哪一个**——**本次未读 `spatial_risk_engine.py`**；**上述算术为本词条自行计算，非作者自述**）。**③ ⭐⭐ **「基线收敛到 1.0×」「最大 3.0×」「λ = 1/300 按危险邻近度校准」三个参数被明确写出**——**其中把衰减率 λ 说成「按危险邻近度校准（calibrated to hazard proximity）」**值得注意：**λ 是一个**可校准的参数**，**而其取值理应有标定依据**（**⚠️ 本词条**不主张** 1/300 有标定依据**——**README 未给出标定数据、拟合样本或来源**；**这是本条目第二处需后续核实的地方**）。**④ ⭐⭐ **技术栈逐字实测且都属地理空间处理的常用组合**：**FastAPI ＋ Pydantic v2**（异步请求处理、请求／响应校验、自动 OpenAPI 文档）；**GeoPy ＋ OpenStreetMap Nominatim**（**并逐字注明使用「compliant User-Agent headers」以符合使用条款**）；**OSMnx** 查询与过滤水文拓扑；**GeoPandas ＋ Shapely** 做投影与几何距离**。⭐ **其中「合规的 User-Agent 头」这一句值得单独记**——**Nominatim 的使用政策要求可识别的 User-Agent**，**把它写进 README 说明作者读过该政策**（**可与本站对**数据来源与使用条款**的一贯关注并读**）。**⑤ ⭐⭐ **示例的请求体与响应体给出了可核对的完整链路**：**请求为 `{"address": "100 Thames Path, London, UK", "base_premium": 1200.00}`**，**响应含 `latitude`／`longitude`／`distance_to_water_meters`（45.2）／`spatial_multiplier`（2.72）／`risk_level`（"High Risk"）／`final_premium`（3264.0）／`formula_applied`**——**即一条**从地址到保费**的完整可追溯记录**（**⚠️ 本词条**不主张**该地址与实际坐标、实际水体距离相符**——**本次未调用其服务**；**⚠️ 另注：示例用的是**看起来像真实地址**的字符串，**而非明显的占位符**）。**⑥ ⭐ **其分级表逐字实测**：**≤10 米 → 3.00×，Catastrophic Exposure（最大洪水加费封顶）**；**11–250 米 → 1.87×–2.93×，High Risk**；**251–500 米 → 1.38×–1.86×，Moderate Risk**；**501–999 米 → 1.07×–1.37×，Elevated Risk**；**≥1,000 米或无水体 → 1.00×，Standard / Baseline Risk（不加巨灾调整）****。⭐⭐ **把连续乘数切成五档并给每档命名，是**把模型输出翻译成核保语言**的一步**；**但对做定价的同学需注意：**分档会重新引入「阈值附近不连续」的问题**——**这正是它开篇批评静态分区的同一种毛病，只是尺度从邮政编码缩到了米**（**此为本词条的判断，非作者自述**）。**⑦ ⭐ **提供一个在线部署（Render）**（**ⓘ 本次未访问**）。**⑧ ⭐ 可与本站洪水与地理风险条目并读**：[[catrisk-sim]]、[[west-bengal-flood-cat-model]]（**本轮同批的另两种巨灾做法**）、[[floodmodeller-api]]、[[lisflood]]、[[thinkhazard]]、[[pyincore]]、[[rfema]]、[[duckdb-fema-nfip]]、[[physrisk]]、[[hazus]]、[[gem-vmtk]]。

⚠️ **如实标注**：**① ⚠️⚠️ **README 声称 MIT，但仓库内不存在任何许可文件****——**README 顶部徽章逐字为指向 `LICENSE` 的「License: MIT」，正文末节逐字为「This project is licensed under the MIT License.」**；**而本词条于 main 分支对 `LICENSE`、`LICENSE.md`、`LICENSE.txt`、`license`、`COPYING` **逐一实测均为 404**，**GitHub API 的许可字段亦报 `NONE`**，**根目录五项中确无许可文件**。**本词条明确记录这一**声明与实际不一致**的情况，并提示：**在使用、修改或再分发其代码前必须自行确认授权状况**（**⚠️ 同批另一候选 [[west-bengal-flood-cat-model]] 亦无许可文件，但**它并未声称有许可**——**本条的问题在于**声称与事实不一致****；**可与第 322 轮 [[saude-publica-br]]、第 326 轮 [[ibnr-app]] 的许可情形对照**）；**②** 本次核实的是**仓库元数据、仓库根目录清单（五项）、README（7,907 字节）全文的问题陈述、四阶段流水线、技术栈、评级公式、分级表、示例请求与响应、以及许可声明**，⭐⭐ **但**未克隆、未安装、未运行 `main.py` 或 `spatial_risk_engine.py`、未调用其在线部署、未读两个 Python 文件的任何一行源码、未核实其公式实现****，因此**不能转述其代码中的实际乘数实现、Nominatim 调用参数、OSMnx 查询细节、Shapely 距离算法或其任何部署行为**；**③ ⭐⭐⭐ **公式不一致已被本词条以算术核实**（见上），**但**本词条不主张**代码里实际用的是哪一个版本**——**这一点的唯一判定方法是读 `spatial_risk_engine.py` 或运行服务，**本次两者都未做****；**④ ⭐⭐ **未核实**衰减率 λ = 1/300 的标定依据**——**README 称其「按危险邻近度校准」，**但未给出标定数据、样本或来源**；**本词条**不主张**该取值有任何经验或监管基础**；**⑤ ⭐⭐ **未核实**其示例中的地址、坐标与 45.2 米距离是否真实**（**本次未调用其服务**）；**⑥ ⭐⭐ **未核实**其分级阈值（10／250／500／1,000 米）的来源与合理性**；**⑦ ⭐ ⚠️ **未评估**该方法在任何辖区的**合规性**——**以地理坐标定价涉及**风险分类的合理性与潜在歧视性定价**等问题**；**本词条**不主张**其可直接用于真实核保或报价**；**⑧ ⭐ ⚠️ **未核实**其对 Nominatim 与 OpenStreetMap 的使用是否确实遵守其使用政策与署名要求**（**README 仅称使用了合规的 User-Agent 头**）；**⑨ ⭐ **实现极小**（`main.py` 18,846 字节 ＋ `spatial_risk_engine.py` 5,475 字节）**——**体量小不等于不完整，但本次无法判断其覆盖了多少边界情况**；**⑩ ⭐ ★0、fork 0**，**关注度极低**，**不主张其成熟度、正确性或已被采用**；**⑪ ⭐ 无 topics、无仓库描述（实测为空）**；**⑫ 是否有中文材料本次未核实**（**README 实测为英文**）。**核实说明**：`https://api.github.com/repos/Devananditha/geo-catastrophe-pricing`、`/readme` 与 `/contents/` 于 2026-09-11 经 GitHub API 实测读取（README 7,907 字节经 `raw.githubusercontent.com` 实测核对；`LICENSE`／`LICENSE.md`／`LICENSE.txt`／`license`／`COPYING` 于 main 分支逐一实测 404）；**两个公式的数值差异由本词条自行计算**（45.2 米处：含偏移 2.7786、不含偏移 2.7203；分级表边界值亦逐点实算）；**未克隆、未安装、未运行、未调用其在线部署、未读任何源码**。
e.body_hk:
**geo-catastrophe-pricing** 是一個**把洪水加費從郵政編碼分區改到坐標到水體距離的定價微服務**（倉庫 `Devananditha/geo-catastrophe-pricing`），**實測 ★0、fork 0、主語言 Python、體量 18 KB、創建於 2026-09-08、最後推送 2026-09-09**（**在解凍窗口內**）；**⚠️⚠️ 該倉庫實測**無任何許可文件**——`LICENSE`、`LICENSE.md`、`LICENSE.txt`、`license`、`COPYING` 於 main 分支**逐一實測均為 404**，**GitHub API 亦報 `NONE`**——**但其 README 卻帶有指向 `LICENSE` 的「License: MIT」徽章，且正文「License」一節逐字聲稱本項目以 MIT 許可發布****；**無 topics**；**README 實測 7,907 位元組**。本條目屬本輪主題**「把假設寫成可核對的東西」**中的**第三種：它把評級公式連同參數一起寫下來，而寫下來的公式與它自己的示例並不一致**。

可核實資訊（**均 README 與倉庫根目錄實測**）：⭐⭐⭐ **根目錄實測只有五項**：**`.gitignore`（291 位元組）、`README.md`（7,907 位元組）、`main.py`（18,846 位元組）、`requirements.txt`（59 位元組）、`spatial_risk_engine.py`（5,475 位元組）****——**整個實現是**兩個 Python 檔案****。**標題逐字「Geospatial Catastrophe Pricing Model | Dynamic Flood Risk Engine」**。⭐⭐⭐ **問題陳述逐字，是最有價值的一段**：**「Traditional Property & Casualty (P&C) underwriting models rely heavily on aggregated territorial rating factors and static postal code boundaries. These coarse macro-level segmentations introduce significant underwriting error: **adjacent structures separated by mere tens of meters can exhibit radically divergent hydrological profiles**, leading to **widespread risk mispricing, adverse selection, and unpriced aggregate exposure**.」**。**四階段流水線逐字**：**物理地址 →（Nominatim／GeoPy 地理編碼）WGS84 點 →（OSMnx 空間圖查詢）半徑 ≤ 2,000 米內水文幾何 →（GeoPandas＋Shapely 度量投影與鄰近計算）最短歐氏距離（米）→（乘數評級引擎）動態保費**；**水文標籤逐字 `{"water": True, "waterway": True}`**；**「若緩衝半徑內不存在任何水體要素，距離按無窮大處理」**；**投影用 `GeoDataFrame.estimate_utm_crs()` 自動確定 UTM 帶以消除緯度相關畸變**。

對 RIAA：**① ⭐⭐⭐ 「相鄰數十米的兩棟建築水文特徵可能截然不同」是寫得最好的一處**——**它把「為什麼需要坐標級定價」講成一個**可檢驗的核保誤差來源****：**靜態分區必然產生**區內方差被忽略**與**區界兩側被強行區分**兩類錯誤**（可與 [[hazus]]、[[gem-vmtk]]、[[floodmodeller-api]]、[[lisflood]]、[[thinkhazard]]、[[pyincore]] 並讀；**⚠️ 不主張**坐標級加費在任何監管框架下都可直接使用**）。**② ⭐⭐⭐ **README 的公式與它自己的示例算的不是同一個函數****。**頭號公式逐字 `Multiplier(d) = 1.0 + 2.0 × exp(−λ(d − 10))`，λ = 1/300**；**示例響應的 `formula_applied` 逐字為 `1.0 + 2.0 * exp(-d / 300.0)`**——**差別正是 `−10` 偏移**。⭐⭐ **本詞條以兩式分別復算該示例（距離 45.2 米）**：**含偏移得 **2.7786**；不含偏移得 **2.7203****；**而示例所報 `spatial_multiplier` 為 **2.72**、`final_premium` 為 **3264.0**（1200 × 2.72 = 3264，自洽）**——**示例實際走的是**不含偏移**的版本，而正文頭號公式寫的是含偏移的版本**。⭐⭐ **分級表亦印證**：**「≤10 米 → 3.00×」這個最大值只有**含偏移**版本在 d = 10 時才能取到**；**而 11–250 米的 1.87×–2.93×、251–500 米的 1.38×–1.86× 與**不含偏移**版本吻合**（**本詞條實算：d = 11 → 2.9280；d = 250 → 1.8692；d = 500 → 1.3778；d = 999 → 1.0716**）。⭐⭐⭐ **即文件裡同時存在兩個函數，而「最大加費封頂 3.00×」屬於**寫了但沒被應用**的那一個**（**⚠️ 不主張**代碼裡究竟是哪一個**——**未讀 `spatial_risk_engine.py`**；**上述算術為本詞條自行計算**）。**③ ⭐⭐ **三個參數被明確寫出（基線 1.0×、最大 3.0×、λ = 1/300）**；**而把衰減率說成「按危險鄰近度校準」值得注意**（**⚠️ 不主張** 1/300 有標定依據**——**README 未給出標定資料、樣本或來源**）。**④ ⭐⭐ e.body_en:
**geo-catastrophe-pricing** is **a pricing microservice that moves flood surcharging from postal-code territories to the distance between a coordinate and the nearest water body** (repository `Devananditha/geo-catastrophe-pricing`), with **measured ★0, 0 forks, Python as the primary language, an 18 KB repository, created 2026-09-08 and last pushed 2026-09-09** (**all GitHub API measurements, inside the thaw window**); **⚠️⚠️ the repository measurably has no licence file at all — `LICENSE`, `LICENSE.md`, `LICENSE.txt`, `license` and `COPYING` each returned 404 on main, and the GitHub API reports `NONE` — yet its README carries a "License: MIT" badge linking to `LICENSE` and states verbatim in a closing section that the project is licensed under the MIT License** (**see note ① below**); it has **no topics**; **the README measures 7,907 bytes**. It is the third of this round’s four takes on **writing assumptions into something a reader can check**: **it writes its rating formula down together with its parameters, and the formula it writes down is not the one its own example applies**.

Verifiable details (**all measured from the README and the repository root**): ⭐⭐⭐ **the root measurably contains exactly five items**: **`.gitignore` (291 bytes), `README.md` (7,907 bytes), `main.py` (18,846 bytes), `requirements.txt` (59 bytes) and `spatial_risk_engine.py` (5,475 bytes)** — **the whole implementation is two Python files**. **The title reads verbatim "Geospatial Catastrophe Pricing Model | Dynamic Flood Risk Engine"**. ⭐⭐⭐ **Its problem statement, read verbatim, is the entry’s most valuable passage**: **"Traditional Property & Casualty (P&C) underwriting models rely heavily on aggregated territorial rating factors and static postal code boundaries. These coarse macro-level segmentations introduce significant underwriting error: adjacent structures separated by mere tens of meters can exhibit radically divergent hydrological profiles, leading to widespread risk mispricing, adverse selection, and unpriced aggregate exposure."** **Its four-stage pipeline reads verbatim**: **physical address → (geocoding, Nominatim/GeoPy) WGS84 point → (spatial graph query, OSMnx) hydrological geometries within a 2,000 m radius → (metric projection and proximity maths, GeoPandas + Shapely) shortest Euclidean distance in metres → (multiplicative rating engine) dynamic premium**; **the hydrological tags read verbatim as `{"water": True, "waterway": True}`**; **"if zero water features exist within the buffer radius, distance is evaluated to infinity"**; **and the projection step uses `GeoDataFrame.estimate_utm_crs()` to pick a UTM zone automatically, so that computing Euclidean distance directly in angular coordinates does not introduce latitude-dependent distortion**.

For RIAA: **① ⭐⭐⭐ The sentence that adjacent structures tens of metres apart can have radically divergent hydrological profiles is the entry’s best-written point** — **it turns "why coordinate-level pricing is needed" into a checkable source of underwriting error**: **static territories necessarily produce both errors — variance within a zone ignored, and the two sides of a boundary forcibly separated** — **and flood is precisely a peril with a very steep spatial gradient** (**readable with the flood and exposure models [[hazus]], [[gem-vmtk]], [[floodmodeller-api]], [[lisflood]], [[thinkhazard]] and [[pyincore]]**; **⚠️ the entry does not claim coordinate-level surcharging is directly usable under any regulatory framework — territory rating has regulatory and statistical rationales in most jurisdictions, including credibility, explainability and the avoidance of discriminatory pricing**). **② ⭐⭐⭐ The formula in the README and the formula its own example applies are not the same function — the point this entry most needs to state plainly.** **The headline formula reads verbatim `Multiplier(d) = 1.0 + 2.0 × exp(−λ(d − 10))` with λ = 1/300**, **while the `formula_applied` field in the README’s own example response reads verbatim `1.0 + 2.0 * exp(-d / 300.0)`** — **the difference being exactly the `−10` offset**. ⭐⭐ **This entry recomputed that example (distance 45.2 m) under both forms**: **with the offset, `exp(−(d−10)/300)` gives 2.7786; without it, `exp(−d/300)` gives 2.7203** — **whereas the example reports `spatial_multiplier` 2.72 and `final_premium` 3264.0 (and 1200 × 2.72 = 3264, internally consistent)** — **so the example actually follows the version without the offset, while the headline formula in the prose carries it**. ⭐⭐ **The tier table corroborates this**: **the table’s "≤10 m → 3.00×" maximum is attainable only under the offset version at d = 10 (`exp(0)` → 1 + 2 = 3.00)**, **while its 11–250 m band of 1.87×–2.93× and 251–500 m band of 1.38×–1.86× match the version without the offset** (**this entry computed: d = 11 → 2.9280; d = 250 → 1.8692; d = 500 → 1.3778; d = 999 → 1.0716**). ⭐⭐⭐ **Two functions therefore coexist in the document, and the claim of a 3.00× maximum surcharge belongs to the variant that is written but not applied** (**⚠️ the entry does not claim which one the code implements — `spatial_risk_engine.py` was not read; the arithmetic above is this entry’s own, not the author’s**). **③ ⭐⭐ Three parameters are written down explicitly (baseline 1.0×, maximum 3.0×, λ = 1/300)**, **and describing the decay rate as "calibrated to hazard proximity" is notable**: **λ is a calibratable parameter whose value ought to have a calibration basis** (**⚠️ the entry does not claim 1/300 has one — the README gives no calibration data, sample or source; this is the entry’s second item to verify**). **④ ⭐⭐ The stack reads verbatim and is a conventional geospatial combination**: **FastAPI with Pydantic v2** (asynchronous handling, request/response validation, automatic OpenAPI docs); **GeoPy with OpenStreetMap Nominatim** (**with "compliant User-Agent headers" noted verbatim**); **OSMnx** for querying and filtering hydrological topologies; **GeoPandas with Shapely** for projection and geometric distance. ⭐ **The mention of a compliant User-Agent deserves separate note** — **Nominatim’s usage policy requires an identifiable User-Agent**, **and writing it into the README shows the author read that policy** (**readable with this site’s consistent attention to data sourcing and terms of use**). **⑤ ⭐⭐ The example request and response give a complete checkable chain**: **request `{"address": "100 Thames Path, London, UK", "base_premium": 1200.00}`**, **response carrying `latitude`, `longitude`, `distance_to_water_meters` (45.2), `spatial_multiplier` (2.72), `risk_level` ("High Risk"), `final_premium` (3264.0) and `formula_applied`** — **a fully traceable record from address to premium** (**⚠️ the entry does not claim that address, its coordinates or the 45.2 m distance are real — the service was not called; ⚠️ note also that the example uses a plausible-looking real address rather than an obvious placeholder**). **⑥ ⭐ Its tier table reads verbatim**: **≤10 m → 3.00×, Catastrophic Exposure (maximum flood surcharge cap)**; **11–250 m → 1.87×–2.93×, High Risk**; **251–500 m → 1.38×–1.86×, Moderate Risk**; **501–999 m → 1.07×–1.37×, Elevated Risk**; **≥1,000 m or null → 1.00×, Standard / Baseline Risk (no catastrophe adjustment)**. ⭐⭐ **Cutting a continuous multiplier into five bands and naming each is a step toward translating model output into underwriting language**; **but for pricing students, note that banding reintroduces the very discontinuity at thresholds the manuscript criticises in static territories — only with the scale reduced from postal codes to metres** (**this is the entry’s own judgement, not the author’s**). **⑦ ⭐ An online deployment (Render) is provided** (**ⓘ not visited**). **⑧ ⭐ Readable with the site’s flood and geospatial risk entries**: [[catrisk-sim]], [[west-bengal-flood-cat-model]] (**this round’s other two catastrophe approaches**), [[floodmodeller-api]], [[lisflood]], [[thinkhazard]], [[pyincore]], [[rfema]], [[duckdb-fema-nfip]], [[physrisk]], [[hazus]] and [[gem-vmtk]].

⚠️ **Stated plainly**: **① ⚠️⚠️ The README claims MIT, but no licence file exists anywhere in the repository** — **the badge reads verbatim as "License: MIT" linking to `LICENSE`, and the closing section states verbatim "This project is licensed under the MIT License."**, **yet `LICENSE`, `LICENSE.md`, `LICENSE.txt`, `license` and `COPYING` each measured 404 on main, the GitHub API licence field reads `NONE`, and none of the five root items is a licence**. **This entry records the mismatch between the claim and the fact explicitly, with the advice to confirm authorisation before use, modification or redistribution** (**⚠️ this round’s [[west-bengal-flood-cat-model]] also has no licence file, but it makes no licence claim — the problem here is specifically that a claim contradicts the repository; comparable to round 322’s [[saude-publica-br]] and round 326’s [[ibnr-app]]**); **②** this check verified **the repository metadata, the five-item root listing, and the README’s full 7,907 bytes in respect of its problem statement, four-stage pipeline, stack, rating formula, tier table, example request and response, and licence claim**, ⭐⭐ **but did not clone, install, run `main.py` or `spatial_risk_engine.py`, call its online deployment, or read a single line of either Python file**, so **the actual multiplier implementation, the Nominatim call parameters, the OSMnx query details, the Shapely distance routine and any deployment behaviour cannot be restated**; **③ ⭐⭐⭐ The formula inconsistency has been verified arithmetically by this entry (above), but which version the code implements is not claimed — the only way to settle it is to read `spatial_risk_engine.py` or run the service, and neither was done**; **④ ⭐⭐ The calibration basis for λ = 1/300 was not verified** — **the README calls it calibrated to hazard proximity but gives no calibration data, sample or source**; **the entry does not claim the value has any empirical or regulatory basis**; **⑤ ⭐⭐ Whether the example’s address, coordinates and 45.2 m distance are real was not verified** (**the service was not called**); **⑥ ⭐⭐ The provenance and plausibility of the tier thresholds (10 / 250 / 500 / 1,000 m) were not verified**; **⑦ ⭐ ⚠️ The method’s compliance in any jurisdiction was not assessed** — **pricing by geographic coordinate engages questions about the fairness of risk classification and potentially discriminatory pricing**; **the entry does not claim it is directly usable for real underwriting or quoting**; **⑧ ⭐ ⚠️ Whether its use of Nominatim and OpenStreetMap actually complies with their usage and attribution policies was not verified** (**the README says only that compliant User-Agent headers are used**); **⑨ ⭐ The implementation is tiny** (`main.py` at 18,846 bytes plus `spatial_risk_engine.py` at 5,475 bytes) — **small is not the same as incomplete, but how many edge cases it covers cannot be judged from here**; **⑩ ⭐ At ★0 and 0 forks attention is very low**, **so no maturity, correctness or adoption is claimed**; **⑪ ⭐ No topics and a measurably empty repository description**; **⑫ whether Chinese-language material exists was not verified** (**the README measurably is in English**). **Verification note**: `https://api.github.com/repos/Devananditha/geo-catastrophe-pricing`, `/readme` and `/contents/` were read via the GitHub API on 2026-09-11 (the 7,907-byte README read via `raw.githubusercontent.com`; `LICENSE`, `LICENSE.md`, `LICENSE.txt`, `license` and `COPYING` each measured 404 on main); **the numerical divergence between the two formulas was computed by this entry** (at 45.2 m: 2.7786 with the offset, 2.7203 without; tier-table boundary values likewise recomputed point by point); **nothing cloned, installed, run or called, and no source read**.
